name: Cedric Belfrage
bio: Cedric Belfrage was the British-born co-founder and editor of the National Guardian, arrested in May 1952 and ordered deported under the McCarran-Walter Act after he invoked the Fifth Amendment before Senator McCarthy. Held about four weeks, he was freed on $5,000 bail and eventually deported in 1955.
charges: Deportation proceedings under the McCarran-Walter Act for alleged Communist/radical affiliation, after invoking the Fifth Amendment before Senator McCarthy.
sentence: Held about four weeks, freed on $5,000 bail; deported in 1955.

name: Mary Beatrice Belfrage
bio: Mary Beatrice Belfrage was arrested in 1953 for deportation over alleged Communist activity years earlier, in a case connected to that of National Guardian editor Cedric Belfrage. Her prosecution was part of the wave of McCarran-Walter Act deportation actions against foreign-born radicals.
charges: Deportation proceedings under the McCarran-Walter Act for alleged Communist/radical affiliation.

name: Boris Sklar
bio: Boris Sklar was the editor of the Russian-language paper Russky Golos, arrested for deportation as an alleged Communist. He was held on Ellis Island without bail under the McCarran-Walter Act.
charges: Deportation proceedings under the McCarran-Walter Act for alleged Communist/radical affiliation.
sentence: Held on Ellis Island without bail; deportation proceedings.

name: Rosaura Revueltas
bio: Rosaura Revueltas was the Mexican actress who starred in the pro-union film Salt of the Earth, arrested by immigration authorities during filming in 1953. She was deported to Mexico that year.
charges: Immigration/deportation — arrested during the filming of Salt of the Earth.

name: Moses Resnikoff
bio: Moses Resnikoff was a foreign-language left-press editor threatened with deportation in 1953. His case was part of a broader McCarran-Walter Act campaign against editors of the foreign-language radical press.
charges: Deportation proceedings under the McCarran-Walter Act for alleged Communist/radical affiliation.

name: Petros Lezos
bio: Petros Lezos was ordered deported to Greece in 1953 despite an earlier grant of asylum. His case was part of the wave of McCarran-Walter Act deportation actions against foreign-born radicals.
charges: Deportation proceedings under the McCarran-Walter Act for alleged Communist/radical affiliation, despite an earlier grant of asylum.

name: Arsen Yerganian
bio: Arsen Yerganian was a 67-year-old Armenian-born man ordered deported to Turkey in 1953. His case was part of the wave of McCarran-Walter Act deportation actions against foreign-born radicals.
charges: Deportation proceedings under the McCarran-Walter Act for alleged Communist/radical affiliation.

name: Reuben Ship
bio: Reuben Ship was a progressive writer handcuffed and deported to Canada in 1953, charged with aiming to overthrow the government, despite having undergone spinal surgery. His case was part of the wave of McCarran-Walter Act deportation actions against foreign-born radicals.
charges: Deportation proceedings under the McCarran-Walter Act for alleged Communist/radical affiliation; charged with aiming to overthrow the government.
sentence: Handcuffed and deported to Canada in 1953.

name: Ethel Linn
bio: Ethel Linn was brought from Canada as a child and arrested in Los Angeles in 1953 for deportation on hearsay of Communist association. Her case was part of the wave of McCarran-Walter Act deportation actions against foreign-born radicals.
charges: Deportation proceedings under the McCarran-Walter Act for alleged Communist/radical affiliation, based on hearsay of Communist association.

name: Stanley Nowak
bio: Stanley Nowak was a former Michigan state senator and labor figure facing a denaturalization suit in 1953, a revived charge of having concealed radical affiliation. The action sought to revoke his U.S. citizenship.
charges: Denaturalization proceedings to revoke his citizenship over alleged radical affiliation.
